title: Article 272 — Taxes levied and collected by the Union and distributed between the Union and the States (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 272 provided for certain taxes levied and collected by the Union and distributed between the Union and the States. It was omitted by the Constitution (Eightieth Amendment) Act, 2000 as part of fiscal reform rationalising tax-sharing provisions. Living Centre–State tax distribution is governed by Articles 268–269A, 270 and related Finance Commission recommendations.
content.glance: Art 272 omitted by 80th Amendment 2000. Tax-sharing rationalised; see Arts 268–270 / Finance Commission.
content.study:
Article 272 was a tax-distribution clause for specified Union taxes shared with States.

Omission: Constitution (Eightieth Amendment) Act, 2000.

Living frame: Distribution of tax proceeds is under the post-2000 / post-GST constitutional scheme (Articles 268, 269, 269A, 270 and Finance Commission).

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 272 as living law.

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Omitted by the Constitution (Eightieth Amendment) Act, 2000. Tax devolution now operates under the reformed Part XII scheme and Finance Commission awards.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 272?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 272 was omitted by the Constitution (Eightieth Amendment) Act, 2000. It is not living law. Current tax distribution is under Articles 268–270 / 269A and Finance Commission recommendations.

examTips: Redirect tax-share questions to Art 270 / Finance Commission / GST framework.
